01-01.title: Italian astronomer Giuseppe Piazzi discovers Ceres, the first object found in the asteroid belt.
The SPT Airboat Line becomes the world's first scheduled airline to use a winged aircraft.
The European Economic Community is established.
Estonia officially adopts the Euro currency and becomes the 17th Eurozone country.

01-02.title: The Soviet spacecraft Luna 1 is launched, becoming the first spacecraft to reach the vicinity of the Moon.
German physicist Rudolf Clausius is born; his work helped establish thermodynamics and the concept of entropy.
Louis Daguerre is traditionally credited with making an early photograph of the Moon using the daguerreotype process.
Two aircraft collide on a runway at Haneda Airport in Tokyo, killing 5 and injuring 18.

01-03.title: The first issue of Berlingske, Denmark's oldest continually operating newspaper, is published.
China's Chang'e 4 makes the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon.
The Mars Polar Lander is launched by NASA.
German mathematician Carl Runge dies; his work contributed to the Runge–Kutta methods used to solve differential equations.

01-04.title: The first issue of the Swedish-languaged Saima newspaper founded by J.
Isaac Newton is born; he later formulates the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
Rose Heilbron becomes the first female judge to sit at the Old Bailey in London, UK.
Spirit, a NASA Mars rover, lands successfully on Mars at 04:35 UTC.

01-05.title: Physicist Max Born dies; his statistical interpretation of the quantum wave function helped shape modern quantum mechanics.
The Daily Mail becomes the first major London newspaper to be published on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean.
US President Richard Nixon announces the Space Shuttle program.
French mathematician Camille Jordan is born; he is known for foundational work in group theory and the Jordan curve theorem.

01-06.title: Sie werden aus Saba alle kommen, BWV 65, a Bach cantata, for Epiphany, is performed the first time.
Mathematician Georg Cantor dies; his work established set theory and transformed the understanding of infinity.
Pan American Airlines becomes the first commercial airline to offer a round-the-world ticket.
Physicist Pavel Cherenkov dies; he discovered the radiation named after him, the blue glow produced by charged particles moving through a medium.

01-07.title: The first American commercial bank, the Bank of North America, opens.
The first transatlantic commercial telephone service is established from New York City to London.
Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency launches Sakigake, Japan's first interplanetary spacecraft and the first spacecraft launched by a country other than the United States or the Soviet Union.
A hot air balloon crashes near Carterton, New Zealand, killing all 11 people on board.

01-08.title: The first Lithuanian-language book, the Catechism of Martynas Mažvydas, is published in Königsberg.
Galileo Galilei dies; his experiments and telescope observations helped lay the foundations of modern physics and astronomy.
Soviet space mission Luna 21 is launched.
Theoretical physicist Stephen Hawking is born; his work transformed the study of black holes and cosmology.

01-09.title: Jean-Pierre Blanchard becomes the first person to fly in a balloon in the United States.
Italian mathematician Maria Gaetana Agnesi dies; her influential calculus textbook was among the earliest mathematical works written by a woman.
Comair Flight 3272 crashes in Raisinville Township in Monroe County, Michigan, killing 29 people.
Apple CEO Steve Jobs introduces the original iPhone at a Macworld keynote in San Francisco.

01-10.title: Computer scientist Donald Knuth is born; he later writes The Art of Computer Programming and creates the TeX typesetting system.
The first great Texas oil gusher is discovered at Spindletop in Beaumont, Texas.
The first General Assembly of the United Nations assembles in the Methodist Central Hall, Westminster.
Astronomer Robert Woodrow Wilson is born; with Arno Penzias, he later discovers the cosmic microwave background radiation.

01-11.title: Astronomer William Herschel discovers Titania and Oberon, the two largest moons of Uranus.
Amelia Earhart becomes the first person to fly solo from Hawaii to California.
The Gateway Bridge, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia is officially opened.
COVID-19 pandemic in Hubei: Municipal health officials in Wuhan announce the first recorded death from COVID-19.

01-12.title: The National Trust is founded in the United Kingdom.
French mathematician Pierre de Fermat dies; he is regarded as a founder of modern number theory.
Dr. James Bedford becomes the first person to be cryonically preserved with intent of future resuscitation.
Deep Impact launches from Cape Canaveral on a Delta II rocket.

01-13.title: The National Geographic Society is founded to promote the exploration and sharing of geographical knowledge.
Henry Ford patents a soybean car, which is 30% lighter than a regular car.
Russian physicist Alexander Popov dies; he was a pioneer in the development of radio communication.
Uzbekistan Airways Flight 1154 crashes while landing at Tashkent International Airport, killing 37.

01-14.title: RMS Oceanic, the largest ship afloat since SS Great Eastern, is launched.
Norway claims Queen Maud Land in Antarctica.
The European Space Agency's Huygens probe lands on Titan, Saturn's largest moon, and sends back images and scientific data.
Logician Kurt Gödel dies; his incompleteness theorems reveal fundamental limits of formal mathematical systems.

01-15.title: Russian mathematician Sofya Kovalevskaya is born; she later makes major contributions to analysis and mechanics.
The Alpha Kappa Alpha sorority becomes the first Greek-letter organization founded and established by African American college women.
Wikipedia is launched as a free online encyclopedia written collaboratively by volunteers.
Yeti Airlines Flight 691 crashes near Pokhara International Airport, killing all 72 people on board.

01-16.title: The Soviet spacecraft Soyuz 4 and Soyuz 5 complete the first docking of two crewed spacecraft and transfer crew members between them.
The League of Nations holds its first council meeting in Paris, France.
An avalanche hits the Icelandic village Súðavík, destroying 25 homes and burying 26 people, 14 of whom died.
Physicist Robert J. Van de Graaff dies; he designed the high-voltage electrostatic generator that bears his name.

01-17.title: Captain James Cook leads the first expedition to sail south of the Antarctic Circle.
Alcohol Prohibition begins in the United States as the Volstead Act goes into effect.
Astronomer Clyde Tombaugh dies; he discovered Pluto in 1930 at Lowell Observatory.
The search for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 is announced to be suspended.

01-18.title: An X-ray generating machine is exhibited for the first time by H. L. Smith.
Japanese-American physicist Yoichiro Nambu is born; he later shares the Nobel Prize for work on spontaneous symmetry breaking.
The International Olympic Committee restores Jim Thorpe's Olympic medals to his family.
Researchers identify the bacterium responsible for Legionnaires' disease, solving the mystery behind the 1976 outbreak.

01-19.title: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's Faust: The First Part of the Tragedy receives its premiere performance.
Scottish engineer James Watt is born; his improvements to the steam engine helped drive the Industrial Revolution.
Mathematician Leonid Kantorovich is born; he later develops foundational methods in linear programming.
The Hong Kong-based file-sharing website Megaupload is shut down by the FBI.

01-20.title: French physicist André-Marie Ampère is born; his work helped establish electrodynamics, and the ampere is named after him.
The first Constitution of Turkey is adopted, making fundamental changes in the source and exercise of political sovereignty by placing it in the nation.
In the United States, the National Negro Network is established with 40 charter member radio stations.
American physicist David Lee is born; he later shares the Nobel Prize for the discovery of superfluidity in helium-3.

01-21.title: Astronomer John Couch Adams dies; he predicted the existence and position of Neptune from irregularities in Uranus's orbit.
The Trade Union Council of Transcarpathian Ukraine is founded in Mukachevo.
Commercial service of Concorde begins with the London-Bahrain and Paris-Rio routes.
French mathematician René-Louis Baire is born; he is known for the Baire category theorem and work in real analysis.

01-22.title: The United Mine Workers of America is founded in Columbus, Ohio.
Physicist Lev Landau is born; he makes major contributions to theoretical physics and later receives the Nobel Prize.
Apollo Program: Apollo 5 lifts off carrying the first Lunar module into space.
French philosopher and astronomer Pierre Gassendi is born; he later becomes the first to observe a transit of Mercury across the Sun.

01-23.title: Insulin is used successfully to treat a patient with diabetes for the first time, marking a turning point in diabetes care.
The First International Opium Convention is signed at The Hague.
Japanese physicist Hideki Yukawa is born; he later predicts the meson as the carrier of the nuclear force.
A very weak signal from Pioneer 10 is detected for the last time, but no usable data can be extracted.

01-24.title: The University of Calcutta is formally founded as the first fully fledged university in South Asia.
Voyager 2 makes its closest approach to Uranus, discovering new moons and rings during the only spacecraft visit to the planet.
Japan launches Hiten, the country's first lunar probe and the first robotic lunar probe since the Soviet Union's Luna 24 mission in 1976.
Swedish mathematician Lars Hörmander is born; his work transforms the theory of linear partial differential equations.

01-25.title: Mathematician Joseph-Louis Lagrange is born; his work shapes modern analysis, number theory and celestial mechanics.
Astronomer Edmond Halley dies; he calculated the orbit of the comet later named in his honour and predicted its return.
The spacecraft Clementine by BMDO and NASA is launched.
A mining company's dam collapses in Brumadinho, Brazil, a south-eastern city, killing 270 people.

01-26.title: British mathematician Arthur Cayley dies; he helped establish modern algebra and the theory of matrices.
The 200-inch Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory sees first light, opening a new era in large-telescope astronomy.
Ranger 3 is launched to study the Moon. The space probe later misses the Moon by 22,000 miles.
Nadya Suleman gives birth to the world's first surviving octuplets.

01-27.title: The University of Georgia is founded, the first state-chartered public university in the United States.
First flight of the Lockheed P-38 Lightning.
Thomas Edison receives a patent for an electric lamp, a milestone in the development of practical electric lighting.
Physicist Charles Townes dies; his work on the maser helped lead to the development of the laser.

01-28.title: Yale Daily News becomes the first independent daily college newspaper in the United States.
The modern LEGO brick design is patented, introducing the interlocking system that defines the toy.
Elvis Presley makes his first national television appearance.
TAME Flight 120, a Boeing 727-100, crashes in the Andes mountains in southern Colombia, killing 94.

01-29.title: Karl Benz patents the first successful gasoline-driven automobile.
Charles Curtis of Kansas becomes the first Native American U.S. Senator.
Pakistani physicist Abdus Salam is born; he later shares the Nobel Prize for work unifying electromagnetic and weak forces.
German mathematician Ernst Kummer is born; his work on number theory includes a major advance related to Fermat's Last Theorem.

01-30.title: The first modern suspension bridge opens across the Menai Strait in Wales.
Physicist John Bardeen dies; he remains the only person to have won the Nobel Prize in Physics twice.
The African National Party is founded in Chad, through the merger of traditionalist parties.
Naro-1 becomes the first carrier rocket launched by South Korea.

01-31.title: Alvan Graham Clark discovers Sirius B, the faint white-dwarf companion of the star Sirius.
Physicist Rudolf Mössbauer is born; he later discovers the recoil-free gamma-ray resonance known as the Mössbauer effect.
United Nations Security Council Resolution 90 relating to the Korean War is adopted.
The Waterfall rail accident occurs near Waterfall, New South Wales, Australia.

02-01.title: The first volume of the Oxford English Dictionary is published.
Physicist Emilio Segrè is born; he later helps discover technetium and the antiproton.
Rear Admiral Lillian E. Fishburne becomes the first female African American to be promoted to rear admiral.
Physicist Werner Heisenberg dies; his uncertainty principle becomes a cornerstone of quantum mechanics.

02-02.title: Chemist Dmitri Mendeleev dies; his periodic table organized the elements and predicted undiscovered ones.
Philosopher and logician Bertrand Russell dies; his work profoundly influenced modern logic and analytic philosophy.
Apple names Gil Amelio its chief executive, a pivotal moment in the company's history before Steve Jobs returns.
Swiss tennis player Roger Federer becomes the No.

02-03.title: The Soviet spacecraft Luna 9 makes the first successful soft landing on the Moon and transmits images from its surface.
Physicist and electrical engineer Oliver Heaviside dies; his reformulation of Maxwell's equations shaped modern electromagnetism.
Space Shuttle program: STS-41-B is launched using Space Shuttle Challenger.
A Baghdad market bombing kills at least 135 people and injures a further 339.

02-04.title: The Codex Sinaiticus is discovered in Egypt.
The United Service Organization is created to entertain American troops.
The social networking website Facebook is launched by Mark Zuckerberg and fellow Harvard students.
Walt Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs opens in theatres, becoming the first full-length cel-animated feature film.

02-05.title: Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte ascends to the thrones of Sweden and Norway.
Belgian chemist Leo Baekeland announces the creation of Bakelite, the world's first synthetic plastic.
Astronauts land on the Moon in the Apollo 14 mission.
Pope Francis becomes the first Pope in history to visit and perform papal mass in the Arabian Peninsula, celebrating Mass in Abu Dhabi.

02-06.title: Jack Kilby files a patent application for the integrated circuit, a key step toward modern microelectronics.
Apollo 14 astronaut Alan Shepard hits two golf balls on the Moon during the mission's lunar surface excursion.
Justice Mary Gaudron becomes the first woman to be appointed to the High Court of Australia.
SpaceX's Falcon Heavy, a super heavy launch vehicle, makes its maiden flight.

02-07.title: English novelist Charles Dickens is born; his works become enduring classics of world literature.
The second full-length animated Walt Disney film, Pinocchio, premieres.
Pluto moves inside Neptune's orbit for the first time since either was discovered.

02-08.title: A patent application is filed for the Harvard Mark I, an electromechanical computer developed by Howard Aiken and IBM.
The Allende meteorite falls in Chihuahua, Mexico; its fragments become some of the most studied meteorites ever found.
French novelist Jules Verne is born; his imaginative adventure novels help shape modern science fiction.
A hotel fire in Medina, Saudi Arabia, kills 15 Egyptian pilgrims with 130 others injured.

02-09.title: Scientists at the University of California, Berkeley, announce the discovery of the synthetic element californium.
The Davis Cup competition is established.
Apollo program: Apollo 14 returns to Earth after the third human Moon landing.
Computer scientist David Wheeler is born; he later contributes to early stored-program computing and the Cambridge computing tradition.

02-10.title: IBM's Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a single game, a landmark for computer chess.
HMS Dreadnought, the first of a revolutionary new breed of battleships, is christened.
Astronomer Edmond Halley is appointed the second Astronomer Royal at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich.
The communications satellites Iridium 33 and Kosmos 2251 collide in orbit, destroying both.

02-11.title: Inventor Thomas Edison is born; his work includes practical electric lighting, sound recording and motion-picture technology.
Anton Bruckner's 9th Symphony receives its first performance in Vienna, Austria.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on a mission to service the Hubble Space Telescope.
The European Space Agency's Intermediate eXperimental Vehicle is launched on a Vega rocket.

02-12.title: Naturalist Charles Darwin is born; his theory of evolution by natural selection transforms biology.
The National Association for the Advancement of Colored People is founded.
Alexander Fleming conducts an early experiment demonstrating the antibacterial action of penicillin in a human patient.
NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft touches down in the "saddle" region of 433 Eros.

02-13.title: UNESCO's World Radio Day is celebrated for the first time, recognising radio's role in communication and public life.
The European Space Agency's Vega rocket makes its maiden flight from Europe's Spaceport in French Guiana.
Apollo Computer is incorporated, beginning the development of influential engineering workstations.

02-14.title: Alexander Graham Bell applies for a patent for the telephone, as does Elisha Gray.
The ENIAC, one of the earliest general-purpose electronic digital computers, is publicly unveiled in the United States.
Voyager 1 photographs the Solar System from beyond Neptune, capturing the image later known as the 'Pale Blue Dot'.
Astronomer James Bradley presents his discovery of the nutation of Earth's axis to the Royal Society.

02-15.title: Astronomer and physicist Galileo Galilei is born; his observations and experiments help transform modern science.
Computer scientist Niklaus Wirth is born; he later designs Pascal and develops influential programming languages.
Sound recordings are granted U.S. federal copyright protection for the first time.
The last Ariane 4 rocket is launched from the Guiana Space Centre, carrying Intelsat 907.

02-16.title: Iceland's first football club, Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur, is founded.
Chemist Wallace Carothers receives a patent for nylon, the first commercially successful synthetic fibre.
The first computer bulletin board system is created.
Archaeologist Howard Carter opens the burial chamber of Tutankhamun's tomb in Egypt.

02-17.title: Thomas J. Watson Sr., who later leads IBM through a period of major growth, is born.
Physicist James Chadwick announces the discovery of the neutron, a fundamental particle in atomic nuclei.
NASA's Discovery Program begins as the NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft lifts off on the first mission ever to orbit and study an asteroid, 433 Eros.
Kosovo declares independence; the declaration is recognised by many countries around the world.

02-18.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn by Mark Twain is published in the United States.
Elm Farm Ollie becomes the first cow to fly in a fixed-wing aircraft and also the first cow to be milked in an aircraft, during a flight over the United States.
Physicist Alessandro Volta is born; his invention of the electric battery gives rise to the unit volt.
Perseverance, a Mars rover designed to explore Jezero crater on Mars, as part of NASA's Mars 2020 mission.

02-19.title: The first group of rescuers reaches the Donner Party.
Astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus is born; his heliocentric model places the Sun at the centre of the planetary system.
China successfully launches the T-7, its first sounding rocket.
The Soviet Union launches the Mir space station, which becomes a major platform for long-duration human spaceflight.

02-20.title: Chemist Robert Huber is born; he later shares the Nobel Prize for determining the structure of a photosynthetic reaction centre.
Italian astronomer Antonio Abetti dies; he made important observations of minor planets, comets and stellar occultations.
Mercury program: While aboard Friendship 7, John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit the Earth.
Spain becomes the first country to vote in a referendum on ratification of the proposed Constitution of the European Union, with voters approving it by a wide margin.

02-21.title: The first telephone directory is issued in New Haven, Connecticut.
Edwin Land demonstrates the Polaroid Land instant camera, introducing a new approach to everyday photography.
International Mother Language Day is observed for the first time, promoting linguistic and cultural diversity.
At least 17 people are killed and 119 injured following several bombings in the Indian city of Hyderabad.

02-22.title: In Utica, New York, Frank Woolworth opens the first of many of five-and-dime Woolworth stores.
Scientists announce the birth of Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.
Saint Lucia gains independence from the United Kingdom.
A ferry carrying 100 passengers capsizes in the Padma River, killing 70 people.

02-23.title: Supernova 1987A is observed in the Large Magellanic Cloud, providing a rare nearby view of a star's explosion.
German archaeologist Reinhard Herbig is born; he becomes known for his research on ancient Greek art and archaeology.
The first mass inoculation of children against polio with the Salk vaccine begins in Pittsburgh.
An Ariane 4 rocket is launched from the Guiana Space Centre carrying Intelsat 904.

02-24.title: Apple co-founder Steve Jobs is born; his products later reshape personal computing, music players and smartphones.
Estonia declares independence, establishing the basis for its first modern independent state.
Pope Gregory XIII promulgates the papal bull Inter gravissimas, introducing the Gregorian calendar reform.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on its final mission, STS-133.

02-25.title: Biologist William Thomas Astbury is born; his X-ray diffraction studies help reveal the structure of biological fibres and nucleic acids.
The SARAL satellite, a joint Indo-French ocean-observation mission, is launched to study ocean circulation and sea level.
Alitalia Flight 1553 crashes at Genoa Cristoforo Colombo Airport in Genoa, Italy, killing four.
At least 310 people are killed in avalanches in northeastern Afghanistan.

02-26.title: The first Christiansborg Palace in Copenhagen burns down.
Robert Watson-Watt and his team conduct a successful radar experiment at Daventry, demonstrating aircraft detection by radio waves.
Apollo program: Launch of AS-201, the first flight of the Saturn IB rocket.
A hot air balloon crashes near Luxor, Egypt, killing 19 people.

02-27.title: The current flag of Japan is first adopted as the national flag for Japanese merchant ships.
The NSA's Harvest computer system is retired after years of specialised cryptologic data processing.
Radio engineer J. S. Hey discovers radio emissions from the Sun, helping establish the field of solar radio astronomy.
French astronomer Bernard Lyot is born; he later invents the coronagraph, enabling observation of the solar corona.

02-28.title: C. V. Raman discovers the light-scattering effect that becomes known as the Raman effect.
Jay Forrester receives a patent related to magnetic-core memory, an important technology in early digital computers.
Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on STS-36.
Prime Minister Modi of India inaugurates the 2nd Space Port of India - Kulasekarapattinam Spaceport.

02-29.title: Abel Tasman's second Pacific voyage begins as he leaves Batavia in command of three ships.
Herman Hollerith is born; his punched-card tabulating machines help lay the foundations of modern data processing.
Hattie McDaniel becomes the first African American to win an Academy Award, receiving the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress.
Luxembourg becomes the first country in the world to render public transport free nationwide.

03-01.title: Yellowstone National Park is established as the world's first national park.
English mathematician and physicist Peter Barlow dies; he is known for mathematical tables, optical work and an early electric motor.
Titanic becomes the first film to gross over $1 billion worldwide.
Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on STS-109 to service the Hubble Space Telescope.

03-02.title: Belgian mathematician Charles-Jean de La Vallée Poussin dies; he independently proved the prime number theorem.
Physicists at Fermilab announce the discovery of the top quark, the heaviest known elementary particle.
Czech Vladimír Remek becomes the first non-Soviet or non-American to go into space.
In Monterrey, Mexico, a man identified as Diego Santoy Riveroll commits a double murder against two children.

03-03.title: Shoshone National Forest is established as the first national forest in the US and world.
Mathematician William Kingdon Clifford dies; his work on geometric algebra later becomes known as Clifford algebra.
Apollo program: NASA launches Apollo 9 to test the lunar module.
Steve Fossett becomes the first person to fly an airplane non-stop around the world solo without refueling.

03-04.title: Physicist George Gamow is born; he makes major contributions to quantum theory and the development of the Big Bang model.
NASA's Voyager 1 reveals Jupiter's faint ring system, the third planetary ring system discovered in the Solar System.
Space Shuttle program: The Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on STS-62.
Nik Wallenda becomes the first person to walk over the Masaya Volcano in Nicaragua.

03-05.title: French mathematician Pierre-Simon Laplace dies; his work shaped celestial mechanics and probability theory.
Cartographer Gerardus Mercator is born; his world map projection later becomes widely used for navigation.
Aeropostal Alas de Venezuela Flight 109 crashes in Venezuela, killing 45.
Pope Francis begins a historic visit to Iraq amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.

03-06.title: German physicist and optician Joseph von Fraunhofer is born; he mapped dark lines in the Sun's spectrum.
Mathematician Ferdinand von Lindemann dies; he proved that pi is transcendental, showing that squaring the circle is impossible.
Ghana becomes the first Sub-Saharan country to gain independence from the British.
Forbes names Jeff Bezos as the world's richest person, for the first time, at $112 billion net worth.

03-07.title: Alexander Graham Bell is granted a patent for an invention he calls the "telephone".
Astronomer John Herschel is born; he catalogued thousands of double stars and nebulae and pioneered astronomical photography.
Physicist Edward Purcell dies; his discovery of nuclear magnetic resonance helped transform physics and medical imaging.
Sweden officially joins NATO, becoming its 32nd member.

03-08.title: Dutch physicist Johannes Diderik van der Waals dies; his equation of state for gases and liquids earned a Nobel Prize.
French aviatrix Raymonde de Laroche becomes the first woman to receive a pilot's license.
The iconic Volkswagen Type 2 "Bus" begins production.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-102, carrying the Expedition 2 crew to the International Space Station.

03-09.title: Physicist Hans Christian Ørsted dies; he discovered that an electric current can deflect a compass needle, linking electricity and magnetism.
Inter Milan is founded on Football Club Internazionale, following a schism from A.C. Milan.
Physicist Walter Kohn is born; he later develops density functional theory and shares the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Space Shuttle Discovery makes its final landing after 39 flights.

03-10.title: The first successful test of a telephone is made by Alexander Graham Bell.
The Courrières mine disaster, Europe's worst ever, kills 1099 miners in northern France.
Syzygy: All nine planets recognized at this time — Mercury to Pluto — align on the same side of the Sun.
The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter arrives at Mars.

03-11.title: French mathematician Urbain Le Verrier is born; using mathematics, he predicts the position of Neptune before its discovery.
In New York City, Samuel Roxy Rothafel opens the Roxy Theatre.
Physicist Nicolaas Bloembergen is born; his work on laser spectroscopy earns him a share of the 1981 Nobel Prize.
Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-123, carrying the first component of the Japanese Kibō laboratory to the International Space Station.

03-12.title: Physicist Gustav Kirchhoff is born; he formulates the circuit laws and helps establish spectral analysis.
Physicist Johann Balmer dies; his formula for hydrogen's visible spectral lines becomes an important clue to atomic structure.
Tim Berners-Lee submits the proposal that develops into the World Wide Web while working at CERN.
A gas explosion in the New York City neighborhood of East Harlem kills eight and injures 70 others.

03-13.title: William Herschel discovers Uranus, the first planet identified with the aid of a telescope.
Physicist John Hasbrouck Van Vleck is born; his work on the quantum theory of magnetism later earns a Nobel Prize.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-29 carrying the TDRS-4 satellite.
Three gunmen attack two hotels in the Ivory Coast town of Grand-Bassam, killing at least 19 people.

03-14.title: Eli Whitney is granted a patent for the cotton gin.
Albert Einstein is born in Ulm, Germany; his theories of relativity reshape modern physics.
Norman Thagard becomes the first American astronaut to ride to space on board a Russian launch vehicle.
Physicist William A. Fowler dies; his research explains how nuclear reactions inside stars create the chemical elements.

03-15.title: Physicist Arthur Compton dies; his discovery of the Compton effect showed that light can behave as particles.
Mathematician James Joseph Sylvester dies; he made foundational contributions to matrix theory and invariant theory.
Symbolics.com becomes the first registered .com domain, marking an early milestone in the growth of the internet.
The 2022 Sri Lankan protests begins amidst Sri Lanka's economic collapse.

03-16.title: Robert Goddard launches the world's first liquid-fuelled rocket in Auburn, Massachusetts.
Physicist Georg Ohm is born; he later discovers the relationship between voltage, current and resistance known as Ohm's law.
A Balkan Bulgarian Airlines Tupolev Tu-134 crashes near Gabare, Bulgaria, killing 73.
Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar becomes the first batter in history to score 100 centuries in international cricket, reaching the milestone in an Asia Cup match against Bangladesh.

03-17.title: Physicist Christian Doppler dies; he described the change in frequency of a wave caused by motion of its source or observer.
Astronomer Friedrich Bessel dies; he made the first reliable measurement of the distance to a star using parallax.
The rubber band is patented in England by Stephen Perry, providing a simple but enduring fastening invention.
The Vanguard 1 satellite is launched; powered by solar cells, it becomes the oldest human-made object still in orbit.

03-18.title: Mathematician Norbert Wiener dies; he founded cybernetics, the study of control and communication in animals and machines.
The opera Leonora by William Henry Fry premieres in Philadelphia, becoming the first known grand opera by an American composer.
Cosmonaut Alexei Leonov, leaving his spacecraft Voskhod 2 for 12 minutes.
Saturn's moon Phoebe becomes the first natural satellite discovered through photographic plates, taken by William Henry Pickering.

03-19.title: Physicist Louis de Broglie dies; his proposal that particles have wave properties becomes a foundation of quantum mechanics.
The Sydney Harbour Bridge is opened.
French physicist Frédéric Joliot-Curie is born; with Irène Joliot-Curie, he discovers artificial radioactivity.
An explosion occurs in Taksim Square in Istanbul, Turkey, killing five people and injuring 36.

03-20.title: The premiere of the very first Romani language operetta is staged in Moscow, Russia.
Physicist Julius Robert von Mayer dies; he was among the first to state the law of conservation of energy.
Libby Riddles becomes the first woman to win the 1,135-mile Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race.
Mathematician Ivan Vinogradov dies; he proved that every sufficiently large odd number is the sum of three primes.

03-21.title: French mathematician Joseph Fourier is born; his work shows how functions can be represented as sums of sine waves.
Astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille dies; he catalogued nearly 10,000 southern stars and named 14 constellations.
Debi Thomas becomes the first African American to win the World Figure Skating Championships.
The social media site Twitter is founded.

03-22.title: The Stanley Cup ice hockey competition is held for the first time, in Montreal, Canada.
The first England vs France rugby union match is played at Parc des Princes in Paris.
NASA's Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on its 16th mission, STS-76.
Two buses crash in Kitampo, a town north of Ghana's capital Accra, killing at least 50 people.

03-23.title: Mathematician Emmy Noether is born; her theorem connects symmetries in physics with conservation laws.
Mathematician Paul Cohen dies; his work on mathematical logic includes the method of forcing.
NASA launches Gemini 3, the United States' first two-man space flight.
The first passenger elevator equipped with Elisha Otis's safety device is demonstrated, helping make tall buildings practical.

03-24.title: Robert Koch announces the discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis.
Mathematician Joseph Liouville is born; he proves the existence of transcendental numbers and makes major contributions to analysis.
Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-45.
Physicist Josef Stefan is born; he formulates the law describing thermal radiation emitted by a hot body.

03-25.title: Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens discovers Titan, Saturn's largest moon, using a telescope of his own design.
Mathematician and surveyor Caspar Wessel dies; he was the first to describe complex numbers geometrically in a plane.
WikiWikiWeb, the world's first wiki, and part of the Portland Pattern Repository.
Protesters demanding a new election in Belarus, following the rigged 2006 Belarusian presidential election.

03-26.title: The first Henley Royal Regatta is held.
Hungarian mathematician Paul Erdős is born; he becomes one of the most prolific mathematical authors in history.
Physicist Anthony Leggett is born; his work on superfluidity later earns him a share of the Nobel Prize in Physics.
Jonas Salk announces the successful results of his polio vaccine, a milestone in the fight against the disease.

03-27.title: Statistician Karl Pearson is born; he establishes influential methods in mathematical statistics, including the correlation coefficient.
Physicist and chemist James Dewar dies; he invented the vacuum flask and was the first to liquefy hydrogen.
Physicist Wilhelm Röntgen is born; he later discovers X-rays, transforming medical imaging.
A Phillips Petroleum plant explosion in Pasadena, Texas kills one person and injures 71 others.

03-28.title: Astronomer Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers discovers Pallas, the second asteroid ever identified.
Palm Sunday tornado outbreak of 1920 affects the Great Lakes region and Deep South states.
Mathematician Alexander Grothendieck is born; his work profoundly reshapes modern algebraic geometry.
Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos begins operation.

03-29.title: The city of Salvador, Bahia, the first capital of Brazil, is founded.
The North American Regional Broadcasting Agreement goes into effect at 03:00 local time.
NASA's Mariner 10 becomes the first space probe to fly by Mercury.
The first same-sex marriages in England and Wales are performed.

03-30.title: Mathematician Stefan Banach is born; he becomes a founder of modern functional analysis.
Chemist Robert Bunsen is born; with Gustav Kirchhoff he develops spectral analysis and discovers caesium and rubidium.
Ether is used as a general anaesthetic during surgery by American physician Crawford Long, a milestone in modern medicine.
SpaceX conducts the world's first reflight of an orbital class rocket.

03-31.title: The Eiffel Tower is officially opened.
Japanese physicist Shin'ichirō Tomonaga is born; his work on quantum electrodynamics earns him a share of the 1965 Nobel Prize.
The Soviet Union launches Luna 10 which later becomes the first space probe to enter orbit around the Moon.
The dwarf planet Makemake is discovered by a team led by astronomer Michael E. Brown at the Palomar Observatory.

04-01.title: Mathematician Sophie Germain is born; her work advanced number theory and the theory of elasticity.
Prince George becomes absolute monarch of the Cretan State.
The TIROS-1 satellite transmits the first television picture from space.
The 2016 Nagorno-Karabakh conflict begins along the Nagorno-Karabakh Line of Contact.

04-02.title: Ludwig van Beethoven leads the premiere of his First Symphony in Vienna.
The ill-fated RMS Titanic begins sea trials.
Physicist Hannes Alfvén dies; his work founded magnetohydrodynamics, the physics of plasmas in magnetic fields.
Gunmen attack Garissa University College in Kenya, killing at least 148 people and wounding 79 others.

04-03.title: The Patriarchate of Friûl, the first Friulian state, is created.
Physicist Ernst Chladni dies; his experiments made sound vibrations visible as patterns in sand on vibrating plates.
The Osborne 1, the first successful portable computer, is unveiled at the West Coast Computer Faire in San Francisco, California.
Apple Inc. released the first generation iPad, a tablet computer.

04-04.title: Argonia, Kansas elects Susanna M. Salter as the first female mayor in the United States.
Mathematician John Napier dies; he introduced logarithms and developed the calculating rods known as Napier's bones.
France announces its return to full participation of its military forces within NATO.

04-05.title: Physicist Ivar Giaever is born; his experiments on electron tunnelling in superconductors later earn him a share of the Nobel Prize.
Tupelo–Gainesville tornado outbreak: An F5 tornado kills 233 in Tupelo, Mississippi.
The Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-37 to deploy the Compton Gamma Ray Observatory.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-131 to resupply the International Space Station.

04-06.title: Mathematician Niels Henrik Abel dies; he proved that general fifth-degree equations cannot be solved by radicals.
Varney Airlines makes its first commercial flight.
Maoist rebels kill 76 CRPF officers in Dantewada district, India.

04-07.title: Empress Matilda becomes the first female ruler of England, adopting the title "Lady of the English".
Mathematician Thomas Bayes dies; Bayes' theorem describes how probabilities can be updated using new evidence.
During STS-6, astronauts Story Musgrave and Don Peterson perform the first Space Shuttle spacewalk.
NASA launches the 2001 Mars Odyssey orbiter.

04-08.title: Theoretical physicist Peter Higgs dies; he predicted the particle later identified as the Higgs boson.
The French Third Republic and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland sign the Entente cordiale.
The Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on mission STS-56.
Bernie Sanders ends his presidential campaign, leaving Joe Biden as the Democratic Party's nominee.

04-09.title: Mathematician Élie Cartan is born; his work shaped Lie groups and differential geometry.
Engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel is born; his projects included the Great Western Railway, the Clifton Suspension Bridge and the steamship Great Britain.
Space Shuttle program: Space Shuttle Endeavour is launched on STS-59.
The Palm Sunday church bombings at Coptic churches in Tanta and Alexandria, Egypt, take place.

04-10.title: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration releases the first image of a black hole, showing the supermassive object in galaxy M87.
Rudolf Vrba and Alfréd Wetzler escape from Birkenau death camp.
The Good Friday Agreement is signed in Northern Ireland.
President of Fiji Ratu Josefa Iloilo announces the abrogation of the constitution and assumes all governance powers after a court ruling invalidates the military-backed government.

04-11.title: Mathematician Andrew Wiles is born; he later proves Fermat's Last Theorem.
An explosion in the Minsk Metro, Belarus, kills 15 people and injures 204 others.

04-12.title: The Froberg mutiny on Malta ends when the remaining mutineers blow up the magazine of Fort Ricasoli.
Sir Frank Whittle ground-tests the first jet engine designed to power an aircraft, at Rugby, England.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-51D to deploy two communications satellites.
Merano derailment: A rail accident in South Tyrol kills nine people and injures a further 28.

04-13.title: The New York City Metropolitan Museum of Art is founded.
Mathematician Stanisław Ulam is born; he co-developed the Monte Carlo method using random sampling.
The United States launches Transit 1-B, the world's first satellite navigation system.
Lion Air Flight 904 crashes on approach to Ngurah Rai International Airport in Denpasar, Indonesia.

04-14.title: The Pan-American Union is founded by the First International Conference of American States in Washington, D.C.
The British passenger liner RMS Titanic hits an iceberg in the North Atlantic and begins to sink.
STS-1: The first operational Space Shuttle, Columbia, completes its first test flight.
The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer is launched by the European Space Agency.

04-15.title: Samuel Johnson's A Dictionary of the English Language is published in London.
Mathematician Leonhard Euler is born; his work shaped analysis, graph theory, mechanics and modern mathematical notation.
Marrakesh Agreement relating to foundation of World Trade Organization is adopted.
Air China Flight 129 crashes on approach to Gimhae International Airport in Busan, South Korea.

04-16.title: The Spithead mutiny begins, immobilising the Channel fleet.
Harriet Quimby becomes the first woman to fly an airplane across the English Channel.
Apollo program: The launch of Apollo 16 from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
Physicist and chemist Joseph Black is born; he discovered latent heat and identified carbon dioxide.

04-17.title: Catalpa rescue: The rescue of six Fenian prisoners from Fremantle Prison in Western Australia.
Physicist Jean Perrin dies; his studies of Brownian motion provided evidence for the existence of atoms.
Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on STS-90, the final Spacelab mission.
Anneli Jäätteenmäki takes office as the first female prime minister of Finland.

04-18.title: Mathematician Lars Ahlfors is born; he became one of the first two recipients of the Fields Medal.
Pierre Laval becomes Prime Minister of Vichy France.
The town of Elmore City, Oklahoma holds its first dance in the town's history.
King Mswati III of Swaziland announces that his country's name will change to Eswatini.

04-19.title: Physicist Pierre Curie dies; he shared the 1903 Nobel Prize for research on radioactivity.
The Jaffa riots commence, initiating the 1936–1939 Arab revolt in Palestine.
India's first satellite Aryabhata launched in orbit from Kapustin Yar, Russia.
The Ingenuity helicopter becomes the first aircraft to achieve flight on another planet.

04-20.title: Physicist Karl Ferdinand Braun dies; he developed the cathode-ray tube oscilloscope and shared the 1909 Nobel Prize.
Mathematician Giuseppe Peano dies; he formulated axioms for the natural numbers and discovered a space-filling curve.
English politician Enoch Powell makes his controversial "Rivers of Blood" speech.
SpaceX's Starship rocket, the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, launches for the first time.

04-21.title: Physicist Percy Bridgman is born; he won the Nobel Prize for research on materials under extremely high pressure.
Soviet forces south of Berlin at Zossen attack the German High Command headquarters.
Baseball: Rollie Fingers of the Milwaukee Brewers becomes the first pitcher to record 300 saves.
Eight bombs explode at churches, hotels, and other locations in Sri Lanka on Easter Sunday.

04-22.title: The first National League baseball game is played at the Jefferson Street Grounds in Philadelphia.
Physicist Emilio Segrè dies; he co-discovered technetium and astatine and shared the Nobel Prize for discovering the antiproton.
Optical fiber is first used to carry live telephone traffic.
The Paris Agreement is signed, an agreement to help fight global warming.

04-23.title: Physicist Max Planck is born; his proposal that energy is emitted in discrete quanta laid the foundation for quantum theory.
The Polish Constitution of 1935 is adopted.
Soviet space program: Soyuz 1, a crewed spaceflight carrying cosmonaut Colonel Vladimir Komarov.
The first YouTube video, titled "Me at the zoo", is published by co-founder Jawed Karim.

04-24.title: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched aboard Space Shuttle Discovery; it is deployed into orbit the following day.
Thorvald Stauning becomes premier of Denmark.
STS-31: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched from the Space Shuttle Discovery.
A building collapses near Dhaka, Bangladesh, killing 1,134 people and injuring about 2,500 others.

04-25.title: Highwayman Nicolas J. Pelletier becomes the first person executed by guillotine.
New York becomes the first U.S. state to require automobile license plates.
Physicist Wolfgang Pauli is born; he formulated the exclusion principle and predicted the neutrino.
Bulgaria and Romania sign the Treaty of Accession 2005 to join the European Union.

04-26.title: Indian mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan dies aged 32, leaving influential results in number theory and infinite series.
Georgios Papandreou becomes head of the Greek government-in-exile based in Egypt.
The British space programme launches its first satellite, the Ariel 1.
Robert Steinhäuser kills 16 at Gutenberg-Gymnasium in Erfurt, Germany, before committing suicide.

04-27.title: Cebu is established becoming the first Spanish settlement in the Philippines.
Inventor Samuel Morse is born; he co-developed the electric telegraph system and Morse code.
Betty Boothroyd becomes the first woman to be elected Speaker of the British House of Commons in its 700-year history.
Israeli archaeologists discover the tomb of Herod the Great south of Jerusalem.

04-28.title: Physicist Arthur Schawlow dies; he co-invented the laser and shared the Nobel Prize for laser spectroscopy.
Wembley Stadium is opened, named initially as the Empire Stadium.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-39, the first unclassified shuttle mission for the United States Department of Defense.
CBS News releases evidence of the Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse.

04-29.title: The galaxy Centaurus A or NGC 5128 is discovered by James Dunlop.
Mathematician Henri Poincaré is born; he founded algebraic topology and contributed to the study of dynamical systems.
Space Shuttle Challenger is launched on STS-51-B.
The wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton takes place at Westminster Abbey in London.

04-30.title: J. J. Thomson announces that cathode rays consist of particles smaller than atoms, later called electrons.
The 1939–40 New York World's Fair opens.
The Iranian Embassy siege begins in London.
Willem-Alexander is inaugurated as King of the Netherlands following the abdication of Beatrix.

05-01.title: Physicist Johann Jakob Balmer is born; he later derives a formula for the visible spectral lines of hydrogen.
Mathematician Peter Lax is born; his work spans partial differential equations, shock waves and numerical analysis.
The Labour Party wins the 1997 General Election and Tony Blair is elected as Prime Minister.
Naruhito ascends to the throne of Japan succeeding his father Akihito, beginning the Reiwa period.

05-02.title: Physicist Heinrich Gustav Magnus is born; the Magnus effect on spinning objects moving through fluids is named after him.
The first game of the Negro National League baseball is played in Indianapolis.
Panamanian general election: Mireya Moscoso becomes the first woman to be elected President of Panama.
Chaitén Volcano begins erupting in Chile, forcing the evacuation of more than 4,500 people.

05-03.title: Edmond Halley's predicted total solar eclipse crosses England and northern Europe; his calculations forecast its path and timing.
Theoretical physicist Steven Weinberg is born; he helped unify the electromagnetic and weak interactions and shared the 1979 Nobel Prize.
New post-war Japanese constitution goes into effect.
The sport of geocaching begins, with the first cache placed and the coordinates from a GPS posted on Usenet.

05-04.title: Mathematician Isaac Barrow dies; his work on tangents and areas anticipated important ideas of calculus.
Italy begins the invasion and occupation of the Ottoman island of Rhodes.
Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on mission STS-30 to deploy the Venus-bound Magellan space probe.
Ken Livingstone becomes the first Mayor of London.

05-05.title: The first edition of The Manchester Guardian, now The Guardian, is published.
The first issue of the Bolshevik newspaper Pravda is published.
Project Mercury: Alan Shepard becomes the first American to travel into outer space, on a sub-orbital flight.
Mathematician Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet dies; he made major contributions to number theory and mathematical analysis.

05-06.title: The Eiffel Tower is officially opened to the public at the Universal Exposition in Paris.
EDSAC, an early practical stored-program electronic computer, runs its first programs at the University of Cambridge.
EDSAC, the first practical electronic digital stored-program computer, runs its first operation.
During a trip to Syria, Pope John Paul II becomes the first pope to enter a mosque.

05-07.title: Alexander Popov presents an early radio receiver to the Russian Physical and Chemical Society in Saint Petersburg.
Treaty of Moscow: Soviet Russia recognizes the independence of the Democratic Republic of Georgia, only to invade the country and establish Soviet rule the following year.
Space Shuttle program: The Space Shuttle Endeavour is launched on its first mission, STS-49.
A China Northern Airlines MD-82 plunges into the Yellow Sea, killing 112 people.

05-08.title: Chemist Antoine Lavoisier dies; his work helped establish modern chemistry and the role of oxygen in combustion.
End of the Prague uprising, celebrated now as a national holiday in the Czech Republic.
The Tollund Man is discovered in a peat bog near Silkeborg, Denmark.
British 17-year-old Isabelle Holdaway is reported to be the first patient ever to receive a genetically engineered bacteriophage treatment, used against a drug-resistant bacterial infection.

05-09.title: The figure who later became Mr. Punch makes his first recorded appearance in England.
Mathematician Gaspard Monge is born; he developed descriptive geometry for representing three-dimensional objects.
Physicist Albert A. Michelson dies; his precision measurements of the speed of light transformed experimental physics.
The May 9 riots following the arrest of Imran Khan in Pakistan.

05-10.title: Physicist Augustin-Jean Fresnel is born; he developed the wave theory of light and designed the Fresnel lens.
Mother's Day is observed for the first time in the United States, in Grafton, West Virginia.
First successful launch of an American V-2 rocket at White Sands Proving Ground.
One World Trade Center becomes the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere.

05-11.title: Theoretical physicist Richard Feynman is born; his work in quantum electrodynamics earned him the Nobel Prize.
Klaus Barbie goes on trial in Lyon for war crimes committed during World War II.
Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on the final mission to service the Hubble Space Telescope.

05-12.title: Mathematician Maryam Mirzakhani is born; in 2014 she became the first woman to receive the Fields Medal.
The Italian-built airship Norge becomes the first vessel to fly over the North Pole.
The Soviet spacecraft Luna 5 crashes on the Moon.
Former US President Jimmy Carter arrives in Cuba for a five-day visit with Fidel Castro.

05-13.title: Mathematician and astronomer Alexis Clairaut is born; he studied Earth's shape and helped predict Halley's Comet.
Three children report the first apparition of Our Lady of Fátima in Fátima, Portugal.
Kosovo War: NATO bombs the village of Koriša, killing at least 87 people.
An explosion at an underground coal mine in southwest Turkey kills 301 miners.

05-14.title: Mathematician John Charles Fields is born; the Fields Medal was established through his initiative.
Lina Medina becomes the youngest confirmed mother in medical history at the age of five.
Skylab, the United States' first space station, is launched.
Agni Air Flight CHT crashes in Nepal after a failed go-around, killing 15 people.

05-15.title: Physicist Pierre Curie is born; his research on magnetism and radioactivity led to the Nobel Prize.
First flight of the Gloster E.28/39, the first British and Allied jet aircraft.
The Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-84 to dock with the Russian space station Mir.
Jessica Watson becomes the youngest person to sail, non-stop and unassisted around the world solo.

05-16.title: Mathematician Joseph Fourier dies; his work on heat flow led to the mathematical technique now known as Fourier series.
The Holocaust: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising ends.
Junko Tabei from Japan becomes the first woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
STS-134, launched from the Kennedy Space Center on the 25th and final flight for Space Shuttle Endeavour.

05-17.title: Archaeologist Valerios Stais identifies a gear wheel in the Antikythera shipwreck material, revealing an ancient astronomical calculator.
Mathematician Heinrich Weber dies; he made influential contributions to algebra, number theory and mathematical analysis.
Malawi holds its first multi-party elections.
Pamir Airways Flight 112 crashes in Afghanistan's Shakardara District, killing 44.

05-18.title: Opening of the first German National Assembly in Frankfurt, Germany.
The first Indian film, Shree Pundalik by Dadasaheb Torne, is released in Mumbai.
Philosopher and logician Bertrand Russell is born; he co-wrote Principia Mathematica and advanced modern logic.
United States presidential election: Joe Biden launches his presidential campaign.

05-19.title: Buffalo Bill's first Buffalo Bill's Wild West opens in Omaha, Nebraska.
The Young Pioneer Organization of the Soviet Union is established.
Space Shuttle program: Space Shuttle Endeavour is launched on mission STS-77.
EgyptAir Flight 804 crashes into the Mediterranean Sea while traveling from Paris to Cairo.

05-20.title: Inventor Emile Berliner is born; he developed the flat-disc gramophone record and improved telephone transmitter designs.
Cuba gains independence from the United States. Tomás Estrada Palma becomes the country's first President.
The first post-Communist presidential and parliamentary elections are held in Romania.
Mamata Banerjee is sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, the first woman to hold this post.

05-21.title: The American Red Cross is established by Clara Barton in Dansville, New York.
The Fédération Internationale de Football Association is founded in Paris.
Mathematician Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis is born; the Coriolis effect describes motion in a rotating frame such as Earth.
A bus accident near Himara, Albania kills 13 people and injures 21 others.

05-22.title: Mathematician and physicist Julius Plücker dies; he contributed to analytic geometry and early research on cathode rays.
Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia and Slovenia join the United Nations.
SpaceX COTS Demo Flight 2 launches a Dragon capsule on a Falcon 9 rocket in the first commercial spacecraft mission to reach orbit and return safely to Earth.

05-23.title: Physicist John Bardeen is born; he is the only person to win the Nobel Prize in Physics twice.
Italy joins the Allies, fulfilling its part of the Treaty of London.
The first version of the Java programming language is released.
A freeway bridge carrying Interstate 5 over the Skagit River collapses in Mount Vernon, Washington.

05-24.title: The First Kingdom of Greece is declared in the London Conference.
Igor Sikorsky performs the first successful single-rotor helicopter flight.
The first Eurovision Song Contest is held in Lugano, Switzerland.
Astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus dies; his heliocentric model placed the Sun rather than Earth at the centre of the planetary system.

05-25.title: Physicist Pieter Zeeman is born; he discovered the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field.
Spanish Civil War: The bombing of Alicante kills 313 people.
The SpaceX Dragon 1 becomes the first commercial spacecraft to successfully rendezvous and berth with the International Space Station.

05-26.title: Charles Dow publishes the first edition of the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
Mathematician Abraham de Moivre is born; his formula links complex numbers and trigonometry, and his work advanced probability.
British Guiana gains independence, becoming Guyana.
Ukrainian-Mediterranean Airlines Flight 4230 crashes in the Turkish town of Maçka, killing 75.

05-27.title: The first group of Dorsland trekkers under the leadership of Gert Alberts leaves Pretoria.
The NC-4 aircraft arrives in Lisbon after completing the first transatlantic flight.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-96, the first shuttle mission to dock with the International Space Station.
The football club Kerala Blasters FC and its first supporters' group Manjappada are formed.

05-28.title: Mathematician and astronomer Milutin Milanković is born; his work linked Earth's orbital cycles to long-term climate change.
The Azerbaijan Democratic Republic and the First Republic of Armenia declare their independence.
The Soviet Kosmos 5 satellite is launched.
Start of the Gezi Park protests in Turkey.

05-29.title: Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico arrives in Mexico for the first time.
A total solar eclipse allows Arthur Eddington's expedition to measure the bending of starlight, supporting Einstein's general relativity.
Space Shuttle Discovery completes the first docking with the International Space Station.
The National World War II Memorial is dedicated in Washington, D.C.

05-30.title: The Kansas–Nebraska Act becomes law, establishing the U.S. territories of Kansas and Nebraska.
Physicist Hannes Alfvén is born; he founded magnetohydrodynamics, the study of electrically conducting fluids.
The European Space Agency is established.
Crew Dragon Demo-2 launches from Kennedy Space Center, becoming the first crewed orbital spacecraft to launch from the United States since the Space Shuttle's retirement.

05-31.title: Mathematician Évariste Galois dies aged 20; his work laid the foundations of group theory.
Second Boer War: The Treaty of Vereeniging ends the war and ensures British control of South Africa.
The Ariane 2 rocket is launched on its maiden flight, carrying Intelsat VA F-14.
The asteroid 1998 QE2 and its moon make their closest approach to Earth for the next two centuries.

06-01.title: French physicist Sadi Carnot is born; his analysis of heat engines laid the foundations of thermodynamics.
The Greek–Serbian Treaty of Alliance is signed, paving the way for the Second Balkan War.
The first international applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty are filed.
Space Shuttle Endeavour makes its final landing after 25 flights.

06-02.title: The first Récollet missionaries arrive at Quebec City, from Rouen, France.
Mathematician Lloyd Shapley is born; his work in game theory introduced the Shapley value and later earned him a share of the 2012 economics Nobel.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-91, the final mission of the Shuttle-Mir program.
Europe launches its first voyage to another planet, Mars.

06-03.title: Liverpool F.C. is founded by John Houlding.
Mathematician Heinz Hopf dies; he was a pioneer of algebraic topology, known for the Hopf fibration and Hopf algebras.
The launch of Gemini 4, the first multi-day space mission by a NASA crew.
The union of Serbia and Montenegro comes to an end with Montenegro's formal declaration of independence.

06-04.title: The Montgolfier brothers give the first public demonstration of an unmanned hot-air balloon at Annonay, France.
Massachusetts becomes the first state of the United States to set a minimum wage.
Tonga gains independence from the British Empire.
Falcon 9 Flight 1 is the maiden flight of the SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.

06-05.title: Physicist Dennis Gabor is born; he invented holography and received the 1971 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Conscription begins in the United States as "Army registration day".
The Bose–Einstein condensate is first created.
The Boeing Starliner is launched on its first crewed flight, carrying astronauts Barry Wilmore and Sunita Williams to the International Space Station.

06-06.title: The Chicago "L" elevated rail system begins operation.
The first drive-in theater opens in Camden, New Jersey.
Physicist Karl Ferdinand Braun is born; he invented the cathode-ray tube and shared the 1909 Nobel Prize for wireless telegraphy.
The launch of SpaceX Starship integrated flight test 4

06-07.title: The newspaper Gazeta de Buenos Ayres is first published in Argentina.
Physicist Joseph von Fraunhofer dies; he discovered the dark absorption lines in the Sun's spectrum, now called Fraunhofer lines.
Sony launches Betamax, the first videocassette recorder format.
The United Nations defines the Blue Line as the border between Israel and Lebanon.

06-08.title: James Madison introduces twelve proposed amendments to the United States Constitution in Congress.
Astronomer Giovanni Domenico Cassini is born; he discovered four moons of Saturn and the gap in its rings now called the Cassini Division.
George Orwell's dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four is published in the United States
The first Venus Transit in well over a century takes place, the previous one being in 1882.

06-09.title: Jacques Cartier is the first European to describe and map the Saint Lawrence River.
Charles Kingsford Smith completes the first trans-Pacific flight in a Fokker Trimotor monoplane.
Astronomer Johann Gottfried Galle is born; he was the first to observe Neptune, in 1846, near the position predicted by Le Verrier.
An explosion kills 17 people and injures at least 46 at a hotel in Peshawar, Pakistan.

06-10.title: The Jardin des Plantes museum opens in Paris. A year later, it becomes the first public zoo.
Physicist André-Marie Ampère dies; he founded electrodynamics, and the SI unit of electric current is named after him.
The Spirit rover is launched, beginning NASA's Mars Exploration Rover mission.

06-11.title: The Limelight Department, one of the world's first film studios, is officially established in Melbourne.
Physicist Charles Fabry is born; he co-invented the Fabry–Pérot interferometer and helped discover the ozone layer.
Diane Abbott, Paul Boateng and Bernie Grant are elected as the first black MPs in Great Britain.
The Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope is launched into orbit.

06-12.title: Mathematician Vladimir Arnold is born; he made major contributions to dynamical systems and singularity theory.
Shooting begins on Paramount Pictures' Dr.
In modern Russia's first democratic election, Boris Yeltsin is elected as the President of Russia.
Kassym-Jomart Tokayev is inaugurated as the second president of Kazakhstan.

06-13.title: Rhode Island becomes the first of Britain's North American colonies to ban the importation of slaves.
Aviator Charles Lindbergh receives a ticker tape parade up 5th Avenue in New York City.
Fahd becomes King of Saudi Arabia upon the death of his brother, Khalid.
Physicist James Clerk Maxwell is born; his theory of electromagnetism showed that light is an electromagnetic wave.

06-14.title: The city of Munich is founded by Henry the Lion on the banks of the river Isar.
Charles Babbage presents his proposal for a Difference Engine to the Royal Astronomical Society, a machine designed to calculate mathematical and astronomical tables.
The European Space Research Organisation is established in Paris – later becoming the European Space Agency.
A Ukraine military Ilyushin Il-76 airlifter is shot down, killing all 49 people on board.

06-15.title: Physicist Alain Aspect is born; his experiments on quantum entanglement later earned him a share of the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Following the 1920 Schleswig plebiscites, Northern Schleswig is transferred from Germany to Denmark.
The Ariane 4 rocket is launched on its maiden flight.
A bomb explodes on a bus in the Pakistani city of Quetta, killing at least 25 people and wounding 22 others.

06-16.title: Physicist and mathematician Alexander Friedmann is born; his solutions to Einstein's equations describe an expanding universe.
Artek, the most famous Young Pioneer camp of the Soviet Union, is established.
Soviet Space Program: Vostok 6 mission: Cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space.
Bhutan becomes the first country to institute a total ban on tobacco.

06-17.title: The United States Navy Hospital Corps is established.
Iceland declares independence from Denmark and becomes a republic.
Nuclear weapons testing: China announces a successful test of its first thermonuclear weapon.
Chemist and physicist William Crookes is born; he discovered thallium and developed the Crookes tube for studying cathode rays.

06-18.title: Astronomer William Lassell is born; he discovered Triton, Neptune's largest moon, and moons of Uranus.
Japanese immigration to Brazil begins when 781 people arrive in Santos aboard the ship Kasato-Maru.
Space Shuttle program: STS-7, astronaut Sally Ride becomes the first American woman in space.
The first Kazakh space satellite, KazSat-1, is launched.

06-19.title: The original Nicene Creed is adopted at the First Council of Nicaea.
The first Father's Day is celebrated in Spokane, Washington.
Garfield's first comic strip, originally published locally as Jon in 1976, goes into nationwide syndication.
The 10,000,000th United States Patent is issued.

06-20.title: Alexander Graham Bell installs the world's first commercial telephone service in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada.
The experimental MW 18014 V-2 rocket reaches an altitude of 176 km.
Cosmologist Georges Lemaître dies; he proposed an expanding universe and an early version of the Big Bang theory.
The Wikimedia Foundation is founded in St. Petersburg, Florida.

06-21.title: The Manchester Baby runs its first program, demonstrating the world's first electronic stored-program computer.
An agreement brokered by U.S. Ambassador Dwight Whitney Morrow ends the Cristero War in Mexico.
Ellen Fairclough is sworn in as Canada's first female Cabinet Minister.
SpaceShipOne becomes the first privately funded spaceplane to achieve spaceflight.

06-22.title: The United States Department of Justice is created by the U.S. Congress.
Mathematician Hermann Minkowski is born; he developed the geometry of numbers and described special relativity using four-dimensional spacetime.
Virgin Atlantic launches with its first flight from London to Newark.
The small town of Elie, Manitoba is hit by Canada's most intense tornado on record.

06-23.title: Mathematician and computer scientist Alan Turing is born; his theoretical machine became a foundation of computer science.
The College Board administers the first SAT exam.
The ocean liner SS United States is christened and launched.
Brexit: The United Kingdom votes in a referendum to leave the European Union, by 52% to 48%.
