USS Enterprise, the world's first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier, is launched.
NASA's OSIRIS-REx capsule containing samples from the asteroid 101955 Bennu successfully lands back on Earth.

09-25.title: The Peace of Augsburg is signed by Emperor Charles V and the princes of the Schmalkaldic League.
Ole Rømer is born; he makes the first quantitative estimate of the speed of light.
NASA launches Space Shuttle Atlantis on STS-86 to the Mir space station.
Bill Cosby is sentenced to three to ten years in prison for aggravated sexual assault.

09-26.title: George Washington appoints Thomas Jefferson the first United States Secretary of State.
August Ferdinand Möbius dies; the Möbius strip is named after this mathematician and astronomer.
Rationing of sugar in the United Kingdom ends.
A mass kidnapping of 43 students from a teaching college occurs in Iguala, Mexico.

09-27.title: Martin Ryle is born; his radio-astronomy methods help transform observations of the universe.
The SS Patrick Henry is launched, becoming the first of more than 2,700 Liberty ships.
The Google internet search engine retroactively claims this date as its birthday.
CNSA astronaut Zhai Zhigang becomes the first Chinese person to perform a spacewalk.

09-28.title: The Declaration of Independence of the Mexican Empire is drafted. It will be made public on 13 October.
Edwin Hubble dies; his observations establish that galaxies exist beyond the Milky Way.
The Democratic Progressive Party becomes the first opposition party in Taiwan.
Falcon 1 becomes the first privately developed liquid-fuel rocket to place a payload into orbit, marking a milestone for commercial spaceflight.

09-29.title: The first practical public electric tramway in the world is opened in Blackpool, England.
Enrico Fermi is born; he later builds the first nuclear reactor.
NASA launches STS-26, the first Space Shuttle mission since the Challenger disaster.
CERN is founded as the convention establishing the European Organization for Nuclear Research takes effect.

09-30.title: Thomas Edison's first commercial hydroelectric power plant, the Vulcan Street Plant, begins operation.
Hans Geiger is born; he co-develops the particle detector that bears his name.
Bechuanaland declares its independence, and becomes the Republic of Botswana.
Hurricane Matthew becomes a Category 5 hurricane, making it the strongest hurricane to form in the Caribbean Sea since Hurricane Felix in 2007.

10-01.title: Yosemite National Park is established by the U.S. Congress.
Chen-Ning Yang is born; his work with Tsung-Dao Lee overturns the assumed conservation of parity.
Pope John Paul II begins his first pastoral visit to the United States.
An independence referendum, later declared illegal by the Constitutional Court of Spain.

10-02.title: By plebiscite, the citizens of the Papal States accept annexation by the Kingdom of Italy.
The "Prelature of the Holy Cross and the Work of God", commonly known as Opus Dei, is founded.
Mathematician Paul Halmos dies; he is known for work in operator theory, logic and clear mathematical writing.
Svante Arrhenius dies; his work explains ionic dissociation and early estimates of the greenhouse effect.

10-03.title: Édouard Lucas dies; he studies the Fibonacci sequence and invents the Tower of Hanoi puzzle.
The Kingdom of Iraq gains independence from the United Kingdom.
Nadine Gordimer is announced as the winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Svante Pääbo is awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

10-04.title: Mexico adopts a new constitution and becomes a federal republic.
Gutzon Borglum begins sculpting Mount Rushmore.
Sputnik 1 becomes the first artificial satellite to orbit the Earth.

10-05.title: Bernard Bolzano is born; his work gives rigorous foundations to mathematical analysis.
The World Series is the first to be broadcast on radio.[citation needed]
Marc Garneau becomes the first Canadian in space.
Lars Onsager dies; he receives the Nobel Prize for discoveries in the thermodynamics of irreversible processes.

10-06.title: Meghnad Saha is born; his ionisation equation explains the spectra of stars.
Opening of The Jazz Singer, the first prominent "talkie" movie.
The first planet orbiting another sun, 51 Pegasi b, is discovered.
Annie Ernaux is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

10-07.title: The Granite Railway begins operations as the first chartered railway in the U.S.
Photius II becomes Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople.
Niels Bohr is born; his model of the atom becomes a milestone in quantum theory.
The Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-112 to continue assembly of the International Space Station.

10-08.title: Ejnar Hertzsprung is born; he discovers a relation between the colour and brightness of stars.
KDKA in Pittsburgh's Forbes Field conducts the first live broadcast of a football game.
Mathematician and engineer Sergey Chaplygin dies; his work advances aerodynamics and gas dynamics.
Thomas Eric Duncan, the first person in the United States to be diagnosed with Ebola, dies.

10-09.title: The Universal Postal Union is created by the Treaty of Bern.
Boulder Dam begins to generate electricity and transmit it to Los Angeles.
Fox Broadcasting Company launches as the fourth US television network.
First lunar impact of NASA's Lunar Precursor Robotic Program.

10-10.title: Henry Cavendish is born; he discovers hydrogen and measures Earth's density.
The Double Tenth Agreement is signed by the Communist Party and the Kuomintang about the future of China.
Mathematician and astronomer David Gregory dies; he is an early promoter of Newton's work.
Sheikh Muszaphar Shukor becomes the first Malaysian in space on board Soyuz TMA-11.

10-11.title: In Washington, D.C., the Daughters of the American Revolution is founded.
Piloted by Arch Hoxsey, Theodore Roosevelt becomes the first U.S. president to fly in an airplane.
NASA launches Apollo 7, the first successful crewed Apollo mission.
NASA launches STS-92, the 100th Space Shuttle mission.

10-12.title: Jeanne Geneviève Labrosse becomes the first woman to jump from a balloon with a parachute.
Piero della Francesca dies; the Italian artist and mathematician writes influential works on perspective and geometry.
Computer scientist Ole-Johan Dahl is born; he co-creates Simula, an early object-oriented language.
The second Chinese human spaceflight, Shenzhou 6, is launched, carrying two cosmonauts in orbit for five days.

10-13.title: First known conversation in modern Hebrew by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and friends.
Bertram Brockhouse dies; his neutron-scattering methods reveal the properties of solids.
France adopts the constitution of the Fourth Republic.
Kurt Reidemeister is born; his moves describe how knot diagrams can be transformed.

10-14.title: Louis Le Prince films the first motion picture, Roundhay Garden Scene.
Benoit Mandelbrot dies; he establishes fractal geometry and popularises the Mandelbrot set.
Apollo program: The first live television broadcast by American astronauts in orbit is performed by the crew of Apollo 7.
The Steve Bartman Incident takes place at Wrigley Field in Chicago, Illinois.

10-15.title: Napoleon begins his exile on Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean.
Tata Airlines makes its first flight.
FORTRAN, the first modern computer language, is first shared with the coding community.
China launches Shenzhou 5, its first crewed space mission.

10-16.title: Girton College, Cambridge is founded, becoming England's first residential college for women.
No. 603 Squadron RAF intercepts the first Luftwaffe raid on Britain.
Yasunari Kawabata becomes the first Japanese person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Lao Airlines Flight 301 crashes on approach to Pakse International Airport in Laos, killing 49 people.

10-17.title: Jacques Hadamard dies; he independently proves the prime number theorem.
Marconi begins the first commercial transatlantic wireless service.
The first commercial nuclear power station is officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II in Sellafield, England.
The 17 October Revolution starts in Lebanon.

10-18.title: Herman Melville's Moby-Dick is first published as The Whale by Richard Bentley of London.
Charles Babbage dies; he designs the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine, precursors to programmable computers.
Félicette, a black and white female Parisian stray cat, becomes the first cat launched into space.
NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Christina Koch take part in the first all-female spacewalk when they venture outside the International Space Station.

10-19.title: Physicist Marguerite Perey is born; she later discovers the element francium.
Astronomers discover ʻOumuamua, the first known interstellar object observed passing through the Solar System.
Niue becomes a self-governing colony of New Zealand.
Hurricane Wilma becomes the most intense Atlantic hurricane on record with a minimum pressure of 882 mb.

10-20.title: Topologist R. H. Bing is born; his work advances the study of three-dimensional manifolds.
British ocean liner RMS Olympic is launched.
Space Shuttle Columbia launches on STS-73.
Harlow Shapley dies; his work shows that the Sun lies far from the Milky Way's centre.

10-21.title: In Boston Harbor, the 44-gun United States Navy frigate USS Constitution is launched.
The first edition of the Ernest Hemingway novel For Whom the Bell Tolls is published.
Fred Dryer of the Los Angeles Rams becomes the first player in NFL history to score two safeties in the same game, against the Green Bay Packers.
Images of the dwarf planet Eris are taken and subsequently used in documenting its discovery.

10-22.title: Clinton Davisson is born; his electron-diffraction experiments confirm the wave nature of electrons.
In East Liverpool, Ohio, FBI agents shoot and kill the notorious bank robber Pretty Boy Floyd.
Space Shuttle Columbia launches on STS-52 to deploy the LAGEOS-2 satellite and microgravity experiments.
India launches its first uncrewed lunar probe mission Chandrayaan-1.

10-23.title: The first National Women's Rights Convention begins in Worcester, Massachusetts.
Ilya Frank is born; he explains Cherenkov radiation and shares the 1958 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Secret police shoot several anti-communist protesters, igniting the Hungarian Revolution.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-120, with Pamela Melroy becoming the second woman to command a space shuttle mission.

10-24.title: Tycho Brahe dies; his precise planetary observations provide the data Kepler uses to derive his laws.
Pierre-Gilles de Gennes is born; he receives the Nobel Prize for work on liquid crystals and polymers.
Deep Space 1 is launched to explore the asteroid belt and test new spacecraft technologies.
The world's longest sea crossing, the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge, opens for public traffic.

10-25.title: Évariste Galois is born; his work establishes the foundations of group theory.
George Lansbury became the leader of the opposition British Labour Party.
Astronomer Henry Norris Russell is born; he co-develops the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram.
Microsoft releases Windows XP, which becomes one of Microsoft's most successful operating systems.

10-26.title: Shiing-Shen Chern is born; his work makes major contributions to modern differential geometry.
Alfred Tarski dies; his work formalises truth in mathematical logic.
Space Race: The Soyuz 3 mission achieves the first Soviet space rendezvous.
Microsoft made a public release of Windows 8 and made it available on new PCs.

10-27.title: Philadelphia is founded in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
The Uzbek SSR is founded in the Soviet Union.
NASA tests the first Saturn I rocket in Mission Saturn-Apollo 1.
Lise Meitner dies; she co-discovers nuclear fission and explains its theoretical basis.

10-28.title: Zygmunt Wróblewski is born; he helps liquefy oxygen and nitrogen from air.
The Alaska Highway first connects Alaska to the North American railway network at Dawson Creek in Canada.
Prospero becomes the only British satellite to be launched by a British rocket.
Mathematician Ulisse Dini dies; his work contributes to real analysis and differential geometry.

10-29.title: Leibniz makes the first use of the long s as a symbol of the integral in calculus.
Turkey becomes a republic following the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire.
The first-ever computer-to-computer link is established on ARPANET, the precursor to the Internet.
China announces the end of its one-child policy after 35 years.

10-30.title: Homi J. Bhabha is born; his work in nuclear physics helps establish India's research programme.
The Communist Party of Australia is founded in Sydney.
Space Shuttle Challenger lifts off for mission STS-61-A, its final successful mission.
First rescue of a prisoner during the Israeli invasion of Gaza.

10-31.title: Nevada is admitted as the 36th U.S. state.
Galileo Ferraris is born; he discovers the rotating magnetic field used in induction motors.
Abraham Wald is born; he later establishes sequential analysis and statistical decision theory.
Soyuz TM-31 launches, carrying the first resident crew to the International Space Station.

11-01.title: Italian Sport-Club Juventus is founded by a group of students of Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio.
The official North Korean newspaper, Rodong Sinmun, is first published under the name Chongro.
The Arecibo radio telescope begins operation in Puerto Rico as the world's largest single-dish radio telescope.
Serbia and Montenegro joins the United Nations.

11-02.title: George Boole is born; his algebra of logic later becomes a foundation of digital circuits and computing.
First day of Battle of Elaia–Kalamas between the Greeks and the Italians.
Capital punishment: Velma Barfield becomes the first woman executed in the United States since 1962.
Expedition 1 arrived at the International Space Station for the first long-duration stay onboard.

11-03.title: Leon Theremin dies; the Russian inventor created the electronic musical instrument that bears his name.
The Koli Point action begins during the Guadalcanal campaign and ends on November 12.
Space Shuttle program: Atlantis launches on STS-66.
The 2020 United States presidential election takes place between Democratic nominee Joe Biden and Republican incumbent Donald Trump.

11-04.title: Rasmus Bartholin dies; he discovered double refraction, in which a crystal splits a light ray into two.
Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming becomes the first female elected as governor in the United States.
China Airlines Flight 605, a brand-new 747-400, overruns the runway at Hong Kong Kai Tak Airport.
The Tigray War begins with Tigrayan rebels launching attacks on Ethiopian command centers.

11-05.title: George B. Selden is granted the first U.S. patent for an automobile.
William Daniel Phillips is born; he later develops methods for cooling and trapping atoms with laser light.
Bill Clinton is reelected President of the United States.
China's first lunar satellite, Chang'e 1, goes into orbit around the Moon.

11-06.title: François Englert is born; his work helps explain how fundamental particles acquire mass.
The 1st Ukrainian Front liberates Kyiv from German occupation.
Cleveland Browns relocation controversy: Art Modell announces that he has signed a deal to relocate the Cleveland Browns to Baltimore, where the team will become the Ravens.
Tammy Baldwin becomes the first openly gay politician to be elected to the United States Senate.

11-07.title: The London Gazette, the oldest surviving journal, is first published.
C. V. Raman is born; his discovery of the scattering effect that bears his name earns him the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics.
NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor.
The Jokela school shooting in Jokela, Tuusula, Finland, takes place, resulting in the death of nine people.

11-08.title: Mary Lyon founds Mount Holyoke Female Seminary, which later becomes Mount Holyoke College.
Felix Hausdorff is born; he becomes a founder of modern topology and set theory.
American pay television network Home Box Office launches.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly announces the withdrawal of ₹500 and ₹1000 denomination banknotes.

11-09.title: The Dublin Society of United Irishmen is founded.
Carl Sagan is born; the astronomer helps popularise planetary science and contributes to the Voyager Golden Record.
Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: An armistice agreement is signed by Armenia, Azerbaijan and Russia.

11-10.title: Elwin Bruno Christoffel is born; the Christoffel symbols become an essential tool in differential geometry and relativity.
Finnish author F. E. Sillanpää is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Luna 17: uncrewed space mission launched by the Soviet Union.
Over five months after landing on Mars, NASA declares the Phoenix mission concluded after communications with the lander are lost during the Martian winter.

11-11.title: Mildred Dresselhaus is born; her research on carbon materials earns her the nickname the queen of carbon science.
Latvian forces defeat the West Russian Volunteer Army at Riga in the Latvian War of Independence.
A vehicle-ramming attack in Zhuhai, China, kills 38 people and injures 48.

11-12.title: Plymouth becomes the first town incorporated by the English Parliament.
The European Space Agency's Philae lander makes the first soft landing on a comet nucleus.
Erdut Agreement regarding the peaceful resolution to the Croatian War of Independence is reached.
The Los Angeles Superior Court formally ends the 14-year conservatorship to pop singer Britney Spears.

11-13.title: Lene Hau is born; her experiments later slow light dramatically and even bring a light pulse to a stop.
Allied troops occupy Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire.
In a referendum, voters in Sweden decide to join the European Union.
A total solar eclipse occurs in parts of Australia and the South Pacific.

11-14.title: Moby-Dick, a novel by Herman Melville, is published in the USA.
Astronomer Gottfried Kirch discovers the Great Comet of 1680, the first comet discovered with a telescope.
Apollo program: NASA launches Apollo 12, the second crewed mission to the surface of the Moon.
The first G-20 economic summit opens in Washington, D.C.

11-15.title: Johannes Kepler dies; his three laws describe how planets move around the Sun.
Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on STS-38, a classified mission for the Department of Defense.

11-16.title: Eugenio Beltrami is born; he builds models of non-Euclidean hyperbolic geometry.
The Jussi Awards, the Finnish film award ceremony, is held for the first time at Restaurant Adlon in Helsinki.
Venera program: The Soviet Union launches the Venera 3 space probe toward Venus.
Space Shuttle program: Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on mission STS-129 to the International Space Station.

11-17.title: H. H. Holmes, one of the first modern serial killers, is arrested in Boston, Massachusetts.
The Tartu Art Museum is established in Tartu, Estonia.
The Soviet Lunokhod 1 becomes the first robotic rover to operate on another celestial body.
Actor Arnold Schwarzenegger's tenure as the governor of California begins.

11-18.title: Elisha P. Ferry is inaugurated as first governor of Washington.
Walther Nernst dies; the physical chemist formulated the third law of thermodynamics.
The first comic of Calvin and Hobbes is published in ten newspapers.
NASA launches the MAVEN probe to Mars.

11-19.title: The second Canadian railway line, the Montreal and Lachine Railroad, is opened.
Mikhail Lomonosov is born; the polymath contributes to chemistry, physics and astronomy, including studies of Venus.
Shenzhou 1: The People's Republic of China launches its first Shenzhou spacecraft.
A double suicide bombing at the Iranian embassy in Beirut kills 23 people and injures 160 others.

11-20.title: New Jersey becomes the first U.S. state to ratify the Bill of Rights.
Willem de Sitter dies; the Dutch astronomer develops an important cosmological solution to Einstein's equations.
The Declaration of the Rights of the Child is adopted by the United Nations.
The 2022 FIFA World Cup begins in Qatar. This is the first time the tournament was held in the Middle East.

11-21.title: Thomas Edison announces his invention of the phonograph, a machine that can record and play sound.
Jacques de Vaucanson dies; the French inventor builds celebrated automata and an automated loom.
The first permanent ARPANET link is established between UCLA and SRI.
A mine explosion in Heilongjiang, China kills 108.

11-22.title: In Dumbarton, Scotland, the clipper Cutty Sark is launched.
Arthur Eddington dies; the astrophysicist explains the energy source of stars and leads the 1919 eclipse expedition.
NASA launches Space Shuttle Discovery on STS-33, a classified mission for the United States Department of Defense.
The Orange Revolution begins in Ukraine, resulting from the presidential elections.

11-23.title: Henry Moseley is born; his X-ray studies establish atomic number as the organising principle of the periodic table.
Johan Alfred Ander becomes the last person to be executed in Sweden.
The first smartphone, the IBM Simon, is introduced at COMDEX in Las Vegas, Nevada.
Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is elected president of Liberia and becomes the first woman to lead an African country.

11-24.title: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species is published.
Simon van der Meer is born; his stochastic-cooling technique helps make the discovery of the W and Z bosons possible.
The D.B. Cooper hijacking begins aboard Northwest Orient Flight 305.
The fossilized remains of Lucy are discovered in Ethiopia.

11-25.title: Édouard Goursat dies; the French mathematician makes important contributions to complex analysis.
Wilhelm Schäfer leaves the Nazi Party and hands over the Boxheim Documents to the Frankfurt police.
Suriname gains independence from the Netherlands.
Jeddah floods: Freak rains swamp the city of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, during an ongoing Hajj pilgrimage.

11-26.title: In the Hawaiian Islands, Captain James Cook becomes the first European to visit Maui.
NASA's InSight lander touches down on Mars to study the planet's deep interior.
France launches Astérix, becoming the third nation to put an object in orbit using its own booster.
The Mars Science Laboratory launches to Mars with the Curiosity Rover.

11-27.title: Also sprach Zarathustra by Richard Strauss is first performed.
Ada Lovelace dies; her notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine include a published algorithm often regarded as the first computer program.
Space Shuttle program: Atlantis launches on STS-61-B, with Rodolfo Neri Vela becoming the first Mexican citizen to travel into space.
Syrian rebel groups led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham launch a ground offensive into Syria.

11-28.title: Russell Alan Hulse is born; he co-discovers the first binary pulsar, providing indirect evidence for gravitational waves.
The Grand Ole Opry begins broadcasting in Nashville, Tennessee, as the WSM Barn Dance.
Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on STS-9, the first mission to carry the European Space Agency's Spacelab research laboratory.
Over seven hundred civilians are massacred by the Ethiopian National Defense Force and Eritrean Army in Aksum.

11-29.title: Mary Somerville dies; the Scottish scientist explains Laplace's celestial mechanics and advances public understanding of science.
U.S. Admiral Richard E. Byrd leads the first expedition to fly over the South Pole.
Atari releases Pong, the first commercially successful video game.
Maurice Clemmons shoots and kills four police officers inside a coffee shop in Lakewood, Washington.

11-30.title: The first-ever international football match takes place at Hamilton Crescent, Glasgow.
Costa Rica signs the Buenos Aires Convention, a copyright treaty.
Jagadish Chandra Bose is born; his experiments demonstrate wireless signalling using millimetre waves.
NASA launches STS-97, the 101st Space Shuttle mission.

12-01.title: President Rutherford B. Hayes gets the first telephone installed in the White House.
Iceland becomes a sovereign state, yet remains a part of the Danish kingdom.
Martin Heinrich Klaproth is born; the German chemist discovers uranium and zirconium and helps establish analytical chemistry.
The outbreak of coronavirus infection begins in Wuhan.

12-02.title: Maryna Viazovska is born; the Ukrainian mathematician later solves the sphere-packing problem in dimensions eight and twenty-four.
New York City's LaGuardia Airport opens.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-53 for the United States Department of Defense.

12-03.title: The first issue of Tamperean daily newspaper Aamulehti is published.
Modern neon lighting is first demonstrated by Georges Claude at the Paris Motor Show.
NASA's Pioneer 10 makes the first flyby of Jupiter and returns the first close-up images of the giant planet.
XCOR Aerospace makes the first crewed rocket aircraft delivery of U.S. Mail in Kern County, California.

12-04.title: The first edition of the Los Angeles Times is published.
Jeremiah Horrocks and William Crabtree make the first recorded observation of Venus crossing the face of the Sun.
The Unity Module, the second module of the International Space Station, is launched.
A firebomb is thrown into a restaurant in the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing 17 people.

12-05.title: New Haven Symphony Orchestra of Connecticut performs its first concert.
The Twenty-first Amendment to the United States Constitution is ratified.
Cecil Frank Powell is born; the British physicist develops photographic methods for studying nuclear processes and discovers the pion.
Exploration Flight Test-1, the first flight test of Orion, is launched.

12-06.title: London becomes the world's first city to host licensed taxicabs.
Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac is born; the French chemist and physicist formulates laws relating gas volumes and temperature.
South Africa grants independence to Bophuthatswana, although it is not recognized by any other country.
NASA reveals photographs taken by Mars Global Surveyor suggesting the presence of liquid water on Mars.

12-07.title: Gerard Kuiper is born; the Dutch-American astronomer discovers moons of Uranus and Neptune and studies Titan's atmosphere.
Australian cricketer Jack Fingleton becomes the first player to score centuries in four consecutive Test innings.
The Galileo spacecraft arrives at Jupiter, a little more than six years after it was launched by Space Shuttle Atlantis.
Aztec High School shooting: William Atchison kills two students at his former high school.

12-08.title: Pafnuty Chebyshev dies; the Russian mathematician makes lasting contributions to probability, number theory and mechanics.
Anarchist insurrection breaks out in Zaragoza, Spain.
The Flag of Europe is adopted by Council of Europe.
Riots break out in Singapore, after a fatal accident in Little India.

12-09.title: The first YMCA in North America is established in Montreal.
Grace Hopper is born; the computer scientist develops early compilers and helps create the COBOL programming language.
Israeli–Palestinian conflict: The First Intifada begins in the Gaza Strip and West Bank.
A volcano on Whakaari / White Island, New Zealand, kills 22 people after it erupts.

12-10.title: The first edition of the Encyclopædia Britannica is published.
Selma Lagerlöf becomes the first female writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi is born; the German mathematician makes fundamental contributions to elliptic functions and differential equations.

12-11.title: David Brewster is born; the Scottish physicist studies the polarisation of light and invents the kaleidoscope.
Apollo 17 becomes the sixth and final Apollo mission to land on the Moon.
The results of the 2019 Bougainvillean independence referendum are announced.

12-12.title: Robert Noyce is born; the physicist co-invents the integrated circuit and later co-founds Intel.
Winter War: The Battle of Tolvajärvi, also known as the first major Finnish victory in the Winter War, begins.
Kenya declares independence from Great Britain.
North Korea successfully launches its first satellite, Kwangmyŏngsŏng-3 Unit 2.

12-13.title: Abel Tasman is the first recorded European to sight New Zealand.
Kristian Birkeland is born; the Norwegian physicist explains the aurora as charged particles guided by Earth's magnetic field.
NASA launches Relay 1, the first active repeater communications satellite in orbit.
European Union enlargement: The EU announces that Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia.

12-14.title: The Glasgow Underground Railway is opened by the Glasgow District Subway Company.
Plutonium is first isolated at Berkeley, California.
NASA's Mariner 2 becomes the first spacecraft to fly by Venus.
Nikolay Basov is born; the Soviet physicist co-invents the maser and laser and shares the 1964 Nobel Prize in Physics.

12-15.title: The United States Bill of Rights becomes law when ratified by the Virginia General Assembly.
The Soviet Venera 7 becomes the first spacecraft to land softly on another planet and transmit data from its surface.
Project Gemini: Gemini 6A, crewed by Wally Schirra and Thomas Stafford, is launched from Cape Kennedy, Florida.
Introduction of the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor into USAF active service.

12-16.title: Virginia becomes the first state to ratify the Articles of Confederation.
Johann Wilhelm Ritter is born; the German physicist discovers ultraviolet light and builds an early rechargeable battery.
The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is enacted.
The Abundant Life Christian School shooting in Madison, Wisconsin, United States, takes place.

12-17.title: First issue of Vogue is published.
Sophus Lie is born; the Norwegian mathematician creates the theory of continuous symmetry, now known as Lie groups and Lie algebras.
The United States successfully launches the first Atlas intercontinental ballistic missile at Cape Canaveral.
SpaceShipOne, piloted by Brian Binnie, makes its first powered and first supersonic flight.

12-18.title: New Jersey becomes the third state to ratify the U.S. Constitution.
Konrad Zuse dies; the German engineer builds the Z3, an early programmable, fully automatic digital computer.
Project SCORE, the world's first communications satellite, is launched.
The United States House of Representatives impeaches Donald Trump for the first time.

12-19.title: Paul Langevin dies; the French physicist develops theories of magnetism and Brownian motion and pioneers ultrasonic detection.
BBC World Service begins broadcasting as the BBC Empire Service.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-103, the third Hubble Space Telescope servicing mission.
Spacecraft Gaia is launched by the European Space Agency.

12-20.title: David Bohm is born; the physicist proposes a deterministic pilot-wave interpretation of quantum mechanics.
Cheka, the first Soviet secret police force, is founded.
The initial production version of the Boeing 707 makes its first flight.
The United States Space Force becomes the first new branch of the United States Armed Forces since 1947.

12-21.title: Apollo 8 launches toward the Moon; its crew becomes the first humans to orbit the Moon and see its far side.
A Thai-Japanese Pact of Alliance is signed.
International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination is adopted.
A Vega C rocket carrying two Pléiades Neo satellites fails after liftoff.

12-22.title: Asteroid 323 Brucia becomes the first asteroid discovered using photography.
Jean-Victor Poncelet dies; the French engineer and mathematician revives projective geometry and advances applied mechanics.
Airborne Express Flight 827 crashes in Narrows, Virginia, killing all six people on board.
A study finds the VSV-EBOV vaccine against the Ebola virus between 70 and 100% effective.

12-23.title: The novel Emma by Jane Austen is first published.
Pierre Varignon dies; the French mathematician applies calculus to mechanics and proves a theorem on quadrilaterals.
First successful kidney transplant is performed by J. Hartwell Harrison and Joseph Murray.
An explosion at the PetroChina Chuandongbei natural gas field in Kai County, Chongqing, China.

12-24.title: Charles Hermite is born; the French mathematician proves that the number e is transcendental.
The first Ariane 1 rocket is launched from ELA-1 at the Guiana Space Centre.
The Spanish police thwart an attempt by ETA to detonate 50 kg of explosives at 3:55 p.m.

12-25.title: Wagner's Siegfried Idyll is first performed.
Ernst Ruska is born; the German physicist designs the first electron microscope.
Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin meets in Egypt with its president Anwar Sadat.
The James Webb Space Telescope is launched.

12-26.title: Thespis, the first Gilbert and Sullivan collaboration, debuts.
Jean Léonard Marie Poiseuille dies; the French physicist and physiologist studies liquid flow through narrow tubes.
Tu-144, the world's first commercial supersonic aircraft, surpassing Mach 2, goes into service.
Orange Revolution: The final run-off election in Ukraine is held under heavy international scrutiny.

12-27.title: Ether anesthetic is used for childbirth for the first time by Dr. Crawford Long in Jefferson, Georgia.
George Cayley is born; the English engineer identifies the forces acting on a wing and helps found the science of aerodynamics.
Apollo program: Apollo 8 splashes down in the Pacific Ocean, ending the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon and return safely to Earth.
Operation Cast Lead: Israel launches three-week operation on Gaza.

12-28.title: Wilhelm Röntgen's paper announcing the discovery of X-rays is published in Würzburg.
Maurice Richard becomes the first player to score eight points in one game of NHL ice hockey.
The United States Endangered Species Act is signed into law by President Richard Nixon.
Indonesia AirAsia Flight 8501 crashes into the Karimata Strait en route from Surabaya to Singapore.

12-29.title: Leopold Kronecker dies; the German mathematician works in number theory, algebra and logic.
Cecil B. DeMille starts filming Hollywood's first feature film, The Squaw Man.
Leaders of the Khmer Rouge apologize for the Cambodian genocide that claimed over one million lives.
The last known speaker of Akkala Sami dies, rendering the language extinct.

12-30.title: Vikram Sarabhai dies; the Indian physicist studies cosmic rays and founds India's space programme.
The Ginza Line, the first subway line in Asia, opens in Tokyo, Japan.
Vietnam War: Operation Linebacker II ends.
A large explosion at the airport in the southern Yemeni city of Aden kills at least 22 people and wounds 50.

12-31.title: Efimeris, the oldest Greek newspaper of which issues have survived till today, is published for the first time.
Robert Boyle dies; the natural philosopher formulates Boyle's law of gases and helps found modern chemistry.
RTÉ, Ireland's state broadcaster, launches its first national television service.
The World Health Organization issues its first emergency use validation for a COVID-19 vaccine.
